To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a continuum level FE model of a partially cement augmented synthetic bone was built based on the subject-specific image data, and the model predictions were in good agreement with experimental measurements.

the stiffness of a trabecular bone augmented with PMMA bone cement can be predicted using continuum-level FE models if a material property conversion is made from the μCT greyscale to mechanical properties of the cement-augmented region, and the mechanical properties of the synthetic trabecular bone.
the stiffness of cement augmented synthetic bone can be accurately predicted in a continuum level FE model using the greyscale related material properties for the synthetic bone and cement regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a subject-specific FE model of a trabecular bone with cement-augmentation.
the development of a subject-specific FE model for predicting the stiffness of cement-augmented synthetic bone using continuum level FE modelling.
the development of a subject-specific FE model for cement-augmented trabecular bone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for cement augmentation modelling, the material properties of the synthetic trabecular bone should be used to define the augmented and synthetic trabecular regions.
, in this study, a continuum-level FE approach was able to accurately predict the stiffness of the synthetic bone and the partially cement-augmented synthetic bone.
the FE models based on the image greyscale related mechanical property mapping were the most accurate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a continuum level FE model of cement-augmented synthetic bone can be built using image greyscale related mechanical material properties.
a more accurate prediction could be achieved by considering the composite nature of cement-augmented trabecular bone.
the continuum level FE modelling is capable of predicting the axial compression stiffness of the synthetic bone and cement composite.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanical properties of the cement-augmented trabecular bone cannot be represented by a homogeneous material.
the mechanical properties of synthetic bone and cement need to be carefully defined to ensure the accuracy of the FE predictions.

it is feasible to model the mechanical behaviour of cement augmented bone using continuum level models, and that the material properties of cement augmented synthetic bone can be determined from the μCT image data.
